$schema_note: Cross-language conformance fixture for the `cognitum-canonical-json-v1` receipt/lineage canonicalization scheme (ADR-0028 D7-D9). Golden values were computed once (see `sha256sums.txt` in this directory for how to regenerate/verify) and are pinned here. Each of the Node, Python, and Rust SDK test suites builds its own native ExecutionReceipt/LineageReference from `logicalReceipt`/`logicalLineageEntry` below, computes its own canonical bytes/SHA-256 digest/HMAC-SHA256 signature independently, and asserts the result matches the pinned `expected*` fields byte-for-byte. This is the test that catches a cross-SDK canonicalization regression (e.g. wrong key casing, inconsistent number formatting, or wrong key ordering) -- unlike each language's own internal round-trip tests, which only ever check a language against itself.
bugContext: Found in independent review of PR #84 (issue #56): Node/Rust canonicalize the signable receipt payload as camelCase (receiptId, contractVersion, subject.requestId); Python's `dataclasses.asdict(r)` emitted snake_case (receipt_id, contract_version, subject.request_id) with no rename step, so identical logical receipts canonicalized to different bytes in Python vs Node/Rust and cross-SDK digest/signature verification failed 100% of the time. A second, independent mismatch was found in the same review pass: Rust's `serde_json` and Python's `json` module both preserve the float/int distinction and render a whole-valued cost amount as `10.0`, while JavaScript's single `number` type makes `JSON.stringify` render it as `10` -- so a receipt with a whole-number cost amount would ALSO fail cross-SDK verification even after the casing fix. `logicalReceipt.costs[0].amount` is deliberately a whole number (100) to exercise this.
_logicalReceiptNote: `usage` is an opaque caller-supplied blob (deliberately mixed-case keys: prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/cacheHitRatio) -- it must be canonicalized verbatim (sorted, but NOT re-keyed) in all 3 languages, proving the camelCase rename only applies to the receipt's own schema fields, never to opaque nested data. `signature` and `verification` are intentionally absent: they are excluded from the signable/digestible payload by all 3 SDKs.
